rationale: The answer is a high-quality, evidence-grounded architecture review. I verified its load-bearing claims directly: config.ts:12/19/35/40 confirms contextIsolation/sandbox/nodeIntegration and webSecurity:false; ipc.ts confirms four channel categories with unknown[]/unknown payloads and the "commits 5-8" header; preload/index.ts:38-68 exposes a bare ipcRenderer wrapper alongside named facades; editor.ts:139-145 and the casts at editorBufferStore/index.ts:189 and app/windowManager.ts:384-386 confirm the restoreBufferId invariant; file.ts:209-216/458 plus store/editor.ts:512-529 confirm the send+push, no-ack save protocol; filesystem/index.ts:25-49 confirms write-file-atomic fsync+rename; editor.vue and types/muya-core.d.ts confirm the engine adapter layer and [key:string]:any boundary; package.json:62, tsconfig.base.json:29/32, electron.vite.config.ts:38/58/84, and types/muya.d.ts confirm the legacy engine is declared but has zero runtime imports (grep found only package.json and a comment). All four domains compare viable options including status quo, with explicit quality-attribute trade-offs, cost, risk, rollback, and consequences of inaction, and a reversible, test-anchored migration path. The two documentation-drift entries the answer flagged (CLAUDE.md config.js/contextIsolation, ARCHITECTURE.md pre-monorepo/muya-JS) are both correctly recognized as stale rather than current, so both are resolved and no decision rests on stale docs. Two minor inaccuracies (unit spec file count, one off-by-one alias line number) do not affect any recommendation; there are no material errors. Current desktop platform is Electron ~42.1.0; the legacy muyajs platform is correctly treated as retired, not current.
